title: Build a small 3D game from a milestone plan with an agent
summary: A game maker says Claude Code built most of Mowtopia, a Unity planet-mowing game, in two days from a 7-milestone plan, with 60 passing tests and AI-made art.
agent_role: Claude Code built the game one plan milestone at a time; the author wrote the plan and generated art, 3D models and audio with image and 3D tools.
outcome: Author reports a working game in two days with 60 passing tests and a 15 MB web build, with art costing about 7,010 credits on the cheapest tier.
what_they_did: The author wrote a 7-milestone product plan for a cozy Unity game about mowing small planets. Claude Code built it one milestone at a time. Concept art and 3D models came from image and 3D generators on Magnific.
how_it_went: They say Claude Code built most of it in two days, with 60 passing tests and a 15 MB web build. A separate three.js game had a first version in 30 minutes from a 7-line plan.
worth_knowing: Turning concepts into 3D models was the biggest cost, about 5,240 of the 7,010 credits.
prompt: Help me build a small [game engine] game: [one-paragraph game idea]. First, write a plan split into about 7 milestones, each with clear goals and tests. Show me the plan and wait for my approval. Then build one milestone at a time, write automatic tests for each, run them, and stop to show me progress before moving on. Tell me which art, models and sounds I need to supply, with file names and formats.

curation.rationale: Gives concrete numbers for an agent-built game and its art costs, but most of the post is a tool list and the build steps are thin.
